summary: The Administration for Children and Families (ACF) is a division of the United States Department of Health and Human Services, headed by a Commissioner and Deputy Commissioner. It manages a $49 billion budget spread across 60 programs serving children, youth and families. The note lists its program areas: welfare assistance, child support enforcement, adoption assistance, foster care, child care, and child abuse.
one_line: Overview of the Administration for Children and Families, a U.S. HHS division running 60 child, youth and family programs on a $49 billion budget.
